newsitem.title: CHINA: China closes investment trust for irregularities.
newsitem.headline: China closes investment trust for irregularities.

text.p: China's central bank, the People's Bank of China, announced on Tuesday the closure of one of the country's largest investment trust houses for irregularities and other serious problems.
The China Agribusiness Development Trust and Investment Corp (CADTIC) had been closed with effect from January 4, the central bank said in a circular carried by the China Securities newspaper.

The central bank had decided to close CADTIC, an investment house under the Ministry of Agriculture, because of serious illegal and irregular business practices that had caused enormous losses, the central bank said.
The decision was also prompted by the recent discovery of serious problems that meant the trust firm was unable to repay debts, the newspaper said.
The trust firm's management had been handed over to the state-owned China Construction Bank, it said.
Priority for repayment would be given to domestic individual creditors, the central bank said. Other creditors would be repaid after the liquidation of the investment entity, it said.

Bankers had said the financial firm that was China's biggest investment trust company after the China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC) had overextended itself due to serious mismanagement.
It had extended its business beyond its officially sanctioned scope -- agriculture -- and suffered large losses from real estate investments and had also invested in securities, they said.
Officials of the China Construction Bank said they were responsible for CADTIC's securities business while its real estate and other investment operations were being wrapped up by the central bank.
The Bank of China had been made responsible for CADTIC's overseas business operations, officials said.
The Hong Kong-based South China Morning Post has reported that senior officials of CADTIC had been detained in Beijing for investigation of alleged embezzlement.
A senior CADTIC delegation, including its general manager, was taken into custody last Tuesday amid allegations of embezzling up to 100 million yuan ($12.05 million), Hong Kong media reported.
The ministries of Agriculture and Finance began an investigation into the financial situation of the company a year ago, an official of the investment company said earlier.
Unlike China's state-owned banks, which can easily attract deposits but face tight restrictions on loans, financial institutions can operate without loan limitations, bankers said.
CADTIC has reported assets of about 30 billion yuan ($3.6 billion) and outstanding loans from such international financial institutions as the World Bank.
